summary: Learn SLOs, observability, incident response, and automation in a practical 5-day SRE course. Build reliability artifacts you can use immediately.
lede: Site reliability engineering (SRE) training covers how teams supporting production services define reliability targets and respond to operational risk. It is for engineers and operations professionals who need to turn service goals and telemetry into practical decisions, including selecting SLIs, drafting SLOs and setting error-budget policies. Learners also practice incident triage, postmortems, observability dashboards and runbooks, and review automation and capacity-planning approaches.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already support production services and need a more structured reliability practice. It fits teams that manage uptime, incident response, observability, and service-level reporting.
prerequisites: Prerequisites required: working knowledge of Linux or Unix-based systems, basic networking concepts such as HTTP, DNS, and TCP/IP, and familiarity with cloud or containerized application environments. You should also bring a laptop and be ready to work with sample incident data, service metrics, and dashboard exercises. No programming certification is required, and coding is not mandatory for completion, although comfort with command-line tools and operational logs will help you get more value from the labs.
